name: illustrator-embedded-image-card
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 2024 (28.6) - Export As > SVG, Styling: Internal CSS, Images: Embed
story: The same guest card as figma-embedded-raster-card - photo, name, role - drawn in Illustrator, which embeds a placed picture as a positioned <image> with a data: URI.
idioms: the placed picture as a POSITIONED <image> with x, y, width, height and a data:image/png;base64 xlink:href - the shape the SVG spec describes and the opposite of Figma's pattern-and-defs indirection
overflow="visible" on the <image>, which Illustrator writes on every placed element
xlink:href rather than href, with xmlns:xlink declared on the root
the layer name on the <image> itself, escaped as _x20_ with data-name holding the original spelling (id="Guest_x20_photo" data-name="Guest photo")
Generator comment naming the SVG Export Plug-In build, root attrs in Illustrator's order with x="0px" y="0px", viewBox/width/height and xml:space="preserve" on tab-indented continuation lines
style="enable-background:new 0 0 1920 1080;" on <svg>, <style type="text/css"> as a direct child with one property per .stN class
a presentation attribute (fill-opacity) sitting beside a class list on the same rect
<text transform="matrix(1 0 0 1 430 812)"> instead of x/y, unitless letter-spacing in a class
tab indentation, one tab per nesting level
whyThisMatters: The picture road has one repro in the corpus and it is a file that FAILS it (figma-embedded-raster-card, sweep finding 2), so the road's own promise in §3 - swap the picture by field, clear it to get the drawing back - has never been measured on a file where it is expected to work. Without that control the finding is unfalsifiable: nobody can tell whether the picture row is missing because Figma writes a pattern or because the picture road is broken everywhere. This is the A side of that pair - same design, same intent, the exporter that writes the plain shape - and it turns finding 2 from "pictures do not work" into the much more actionable "pictures work, and Figma's pattern indirection is what hides them".
